lines: See this tiny hole in your airplane window?
It's not a crack. It's called a breather hole.
First problem? Fog. Moisture gets trapped between the panes.
And at [35,000|thirty-five thousand] feet, it's about [-50°C|minus fifty degrees] outside.
So it freezes. Goodbye, window seat.
Second problem. Your window actually has three layers.
The hole keeps the air pressure equal around the middle pane, so only the outer pane takes the load.
The middle pane just chills. It's the backup.
Without the hole, the middle pane would share the strain on every flight.
Your backup... wouldn't be fresh anymore.
So next time you see that tiny hole, relax. It means your window is doing its job.
So... what should I delete next?
